# Concepts

Herdr is a terminal workspace manager. It keeps real terminal processes running and adds structure around them.

## Workspace

[![SVG Image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Section titled “Workspace”](#workspace)

A workspace is the top-level project container. Use one workspace per repo, task, or investigation.

A workspace owns tabs and panes. Its sidebar state rolls up from the agents inside it, so you can see which project needs attention.

## Tab

[![SVG Image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Section titled “Tab”](#tab)

A tab is a layout inside a workspace. Use tabs to separate views like `agents`, `logs`, `server`, or `review`.

Tabs are addressable from the CLI and socket API.

## Pane

[![SVG Image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Section titled “Pane”](#pane)

A pane is a real terminal. Herdr renders the terminal output, sends input back to the process, and preserves the pane across client detach.

Panes can be split right or down. They can be renamed manually, read from the CLI, sent input, and closed.

## Mouse UI

[![SVG Image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Section titled “Mouse UI”](#mouse-ui)

Herdr is mouse-native. You can click panes, tabs, workspaces, and agents. You can drag split borders, select text, and use right-click menus. Everything below is also reachable by mouse; keyboard bindings are an optional layer.

If you prefer keyboard-only control, or you want Herdr to stop capturing mouse input, disable mouse capture:

    [ui]

    mouse_capture = false

## Agent

[![SVG Image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Section titled “Agent”](#agent)

An agent is a process Herdr recognizes inside a pane. Herdr detects agents from foreground processes, screen manifests, and optional integrations.

Agent states are:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `blocked` | The agent needs input, approval, or a decision. |
| `working` | The agent is actively running. |
| `done` | The agent finished and you have not looked at it yet. |
| `idle` | The agent is finished or waiting and has been seen. |
| `unknown` | Herdr cannot confidently classify the state. |

## Session

[![SVG Image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Section titled “Session”](#session)

A session is a persistent Herdr server namespace. The default `herdr` command attaches to the default session.

Named sessions are separate runtime namespaces:

Terminal window

    herdr session list

    herdr session attach work

    herdr session attach side-project

Use workspaces first. Use named sessions when you need completely separate panes, sockets, and persisted runtime state.

## Client and server

[![SVG Image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Section titled “Client and server”](#client-and-server)

By default, Herdr runs as a background server plus one or more attached clients.

The server owns panes and process state. The client is the terminal UI attached to that server.

Detach the client with `ctrl+b q`. The server and agents continue running.

If you want to end the session and stop its panes, stop the server:

Terminal window

    herdr server stop

## Modes

[![SVG Image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Section titled “Modes”](#modes)

Herdr has terminal mode, prefix mode, and navigate mode.

Terminal mode sends keys to the focused pane. Prefix mode waits for one Herdr action after the prefix key. Navigate mode is the persistent workspace navigation surface.

Press the prefix key, default `ctrl+b`, then an action key such as `c` for a new tab or `w` for workspace navigation. New to the prefix idea? See [Keyboard](/docs/keyboard/).

content.text:
## Why ALT, not SUPER

Two independent reasons, both concrete:

1. **Hyprland (the compositor) already owns SUPER extensively** — `SUPER+F` (yazi), `SUPER+1-9` (workspaces), `SUPER+Q/D/arrows` (window mgmt), `SUPER+SHIFT+1-9` (move to workspace), etc. Any new `SUPER+X` for herdr risks colliding with something already bound at the compositor level — and compositor-level interception happens *before* the keypress even reaches ghostty/herdr, so there's no way to "win" that race the way we could for `--gtk-single-instance=false`.
2. **Ghostty itself already claims `super+shift+*`** for its own pane splitting (`new_split`, `close_surface`, `goto_split:up/down/left/right`, `toggle_maximize`) — the exact conflict class that started this whole herdr-keybind thread. Since herdr runs nested inside ghostty, ghostty eats those first.

`Alt+Shift` was empirically verified clear at both layers for every chord we've bound. `Super+anything` is genuinely riskier here, not just a style choice — happy to hunt for a specific free `Super+Shift+X` if you want one, but it won't have the same blanket safety.

## Moving between tabs

Confirmed defaults (from the config reference):

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl+B` then `P` | Previous tab |
| `Ctrl+B` then `N` | Next tab |
| `Ctrl+B` then `1`-`9` | Jump to tab by number |

Want direct `Alt+Shift` chords added, matching our pattern? Herdr's own docs literally recommend bracket-pair chords for this exact purpose (`previous_tab = ["prefix+p", "ctrl+alt+["]`, `next_tab = [..., "ctrl+alt+]"]`). Let me check `Alt+Shift+[` / `Alt+Shift+]` for conflicts before proposing.

# Direct (non-prefix) alt+shift chords mirroring ghostty's goto_split
# P/;/L/' keys exactly, since ghostty runs as the host terminal and
# intercepts super+shift+* before herdr ever sees it. Verified against
# ghostty's full resolved keybinds (`ghostty +show-config`, defaults
# included) and Hyprland's active binds (`hyprctl binds`) - neither claims
# these exact alt+shift chords. Raw punctuation is valid herdr key syntax
# (the built-in default copy_mode = "prefix+[" uses a literal bracket);
# only characters that collide with the binding grammar itself (+, -, etc.)
# need named tokens (minus, comma, backtick, ...).
[keys]
split_vertical   = "alt+shift+enter"  # side-by-side (confirmed via docs: "split vertically" = right split)
close_pane       = "alt+shift+\\"
zoom             = "alt+shift+f"
settings         = "alt+shift+o"
focus_pane_up    = "alt+shift+p"
focus_pane_down  = "alt+shift+;"
focus_pane_left  = "alt+shift+l"
focus_pane_right = "alt+shift+'"

# Prefix-free direct chord added alongside the default "prefix+w" (kept as
# fallback per herdr's own recommended prefix-free pattern).
workspace_picker = ["prefix+w", "alt+shift+w"]

# Tab switching, mirroring the bracket-pair pattern herdr's own docs use
# for prefix-free tab chords ("ctrl+alt+[" / "ctrl+alt+]" in their example).
previous_tab = ["prefix+p", "alt+shift+["]
next_tab     = ["prefix+n", "alt+shift+]"]

# Workspace cycling, unset by default. Comma/period mirrors the previous/next
# convention used above for tabs, completing pane -> tab -> workspace symmetry.
previous_workspace = "alt+shift+comma"
next_workspace      = "alt+shift+."

# ctrl+shift+c is currently shadowed by ghostty's copy_to_clipboard while
# herdr runs nested inside it (ghostty intercepts first) - kept for parity
# and for if herdr ever runs under a host that doesn't bind it.
copy_mode        = "ctrl+shift+c"

# No paste action exists in herdr's keybind action set; ghostty's
# ctrl+shift+v already delivers pasted text into the focused pane.

#     switching replaces it; this was a compositor-level intercept, one
#     layer below ghostty, so it would have blocked the keypress entirely)
# Verified conflict-free after removal via `ghostty +show-config` and
# `hyprctl binds`.
[keys]
split_vertical   = "alt+shift+enter"  # side-by-side (confirmed via docs: "split vertically" = right split)
close_pane       = "alt+shift+\\"
zoom             = "alt+shift+f"

next_tab     = "ctrl+super+'"

next_workspace      = "ctrl+super+;"

# herdr runs nested inside it (ghostty intercepts first) - kept for parity
# and for if herdr ever runs under a host that doesn't bind it.
copy_mode        = "ctrl+shift+c"

# No paste action exists in herdr's keybind action set; ghostty's
# ctrl+shift+v already delivers pasted text into the focused pane.

  hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.exec_raw("pin"))

6:# Three-tier scheme, all direct (non-prefix) chords:
7:#   SHIFT+SUPER  = panes    (P/;/L/' = up/down/left/right, matches ghostty's
8:#                  old goto_split layout)
9:#   CTRL+SUPER   = tabs (L/') and workspaces (P/;), reusing the same four
10:#                  letters as panes via a different modifier
11:#   CTRL+SUPER+G = search/goto across tabs and workspaces
12:#
13:# These exact chords collided with two things that had to be freed up first:
14:#   - ghostty's own super+shift+P/;/L/'=goto_split:* (removed from
15:#     ~/.config/ghostty/config - herdr's pane focus replaces it)
16:#   - Hyprland's own SUPER+CTRL+L/apostrophe/P/semicolon window-swap binds
17:#     (removed from ~/.config/hypr/conf/keybinds.lua - herdr's tab/workspace
18:#     switching replaces it; this was a compositor-level intercept, one
19:#     layer below ghostty, so it would have blocked the keypress entirely)
20:# Verified conflict-free after removal via `ghostty +show-config` and
21:# `hyprctl binds`.
22:[keys]
23:split_vertical   = "alt+shift+enter"  # side-by-side (confirmed via docs: "split vertically" = right split)

local vars = require("conf.vars")
local modKey = "SUPER"

-- ============================================================
--  APPLICATIONS  (SUPER + SHIFT = launch)
-- ============================================================
hl.bind(modKey .. " + RETURN",         hl.dsp.exec_cmd(vars.terminal))

hl.bind(modKey .. " + B",      hl.dsp.exec_cmd(vars.browser))

  hl.exec_cmd(vars.browser)
  hl.exec_cmd(vars.terminal)
end)

---- Scroll -------------------------------------------------------
-- hl.bind("ALT + semicolon", hl.dsp.scroll({ direction = "down" }))
hl.bind("ALT + P", function() 
  hl.exec_cmd("move +col")
end)

-- ============================================================
--  WINDOW MANAGEMENT  (SUPER)
-- ============================================================
hl.bind(modKey .. " + Q", hl.dsp.window.close())                     -- close window
hl.bind(modKey .. " + D", hl.dsp.window.float({ action = "toggle" })) -- toggle float

hl.bind(modKey .. " + bracketright", hl.dsp.window.fullscreen({ mode = 0 }))    -- fullscreen

-- Pop out: float + size + center + pin  (Omarchy's SUPER+O)
hl.bind(modKey .. " + O", function()

…

end)

-- Toggle whole-workspace layout dwindle <-> master  (Omarchy's SUPER+L)
hl.bind(modKey .. " + N", function()
  if hl.get_config("general.layout") == "dwindle" then
…
  end
end)

-- ---- Focus / swap / cycle ----------------------------------
hl.bind(modKey  .. " + L",  hl.dsp.focus({ direction = "l" }))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + apostrophe", hl.dsp.focus({ direction = "r" }))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + P",    hl.dsp.focus({ direction = "u" }))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + semicolon",  hl.dsp.focus({ direction = "d" }))


-- ---- Resize (horizontal, Omarchy default) ------------------
hl.bind(modKey .. " + minus", hl.dsp.window.resize({ x = 100*(16/9), y = 100, relative = true }))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + equal", hl.dsp.window.resize({ x = -100*(16/9), y = -100, relative = true }))

-- ---- Mouse move / resize -----------------------------------

for i = 1, 9 do

    hl.bind(modKey .. " + SHIFT + " .. i, hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = i }))
    hl.bind(modKey .. " + SHIFT + ALT + " .. i, hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = i, silent = true }))
end

hl.bind(modKey .. " + ALT + 0", hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = 10 }))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + SHIFT + ALT + 0", hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = 10, silent = true }))
-- ---- Scratchpad --------------------------------------------
hl.bind(modKey .. " + S",       hl.dsp.workspace.toggle_special("scratchpad"))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + ALT + S", hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = "special:scratchpad" }))

--  SYSTEM / SETTINGS  (SUPER + CTRL)  — mapped to standard tools
-- ============================================================
-- hl.bind(modKey .. " + CTRL + L", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("hyprlock"))                     -- lock
hl.bind(modKey .. " + CTRL + A", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("pavucontrol"))                  -- audio
hl.bind(modKey .. " + CTRL + B", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("blueman-manager"))              -- bluetooth

-- Wallpaper -> transition map (keyed by filename). Files not listed here use

Confirmed: `F` is now only at `modmask 64` (bare SUPER+F = yazi, unchanged) and `modmask 69` (relocated nautilus). `modmask 65` (SUPER+SHIFT+F) is free for herdr's search.

## Workspace naming
`ui.prompt_new_workspace_name` defaults to `false` (tabs default `true`, workspaces don't — asymmetric by design in herdr). Flipped it on.

## New keys

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `Super+Shift+T` | Close tab |
| `Super+Shift+W` | Close workspace |
| `Super+Shift+F` | Search (session navigator, replaces `Ctrl+Super+W`) |

## What had to move (nothing lost, all relocated)

- Ghostty's `super+shift+F=toggle_maximize` — **removed**, not relocated. Redundant with herdr's own `zoom`.
- Hyprland's `SUPER+SHIFT+F` (nautilus GUI file manager) → **`Ctrl+Super+Shift+F`**.

## Important — I also found and fixed a real problem

**Every custom ghostty keybind was silently commented out** in the config file (`# keybind = ...` on every line) when I went to check it — not something I did. I don't know the exact cause (possibly the `Ctrl+Shift+,` reload path, possibly something else), but it meant *none* of this session's ghostty customizations were actually active. I rebuilt the file from scratch with only what's still needed: `super+shift+O` (command palette, no herdr equivalent), `jump_to_prompt`, and clipboard copy/paste. Everything superseded by herdr (splits, close, zoom, pane-goto) is gone for good this time, not just commented.

**You need `Ctrl+Shift+,` (or a full ghostty restart) again** for this rebuilt file to take effect — same requirement as before, now with a clean file underneath it.
